title: Anne Brontë's birth chart
metaDescription: Anne Brontë's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.4° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: the Sun and Saturn within 0.2°, identity wired to structure. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 26.4° Capricorn — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mercury. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Capricorn and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (3.0°), Venus in Aquarius (20.5°), Mars in Cancer (25.5°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Saturn is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.2°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Mars trine Pluto at 0.3°, and Saturn square Uranus at 0.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, one sits in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Cancer at 25.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 air, 3 water, 2 earth, 2 fire by element and 4 mutable, 3 cardinal, 3 fixed by mode. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Mars was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 15.1° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 21.7°.
